name: composio-event-trigger-debug
description: "How to debug event-triggered automations that never fire on cloud; Composio signs webhooks v1,base64 (fixed in PR #7168, 2026-09-26)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory

Event-triggered automations (Composio triggers) silently did nothing on cloud because ingress `POST /triggers/composio/events/` returned 401 for every delivery: we checked a hex HMAC, Composio sends Standard Webhooks `v1,<base64>` (see Composio SDK `verify_webhook`). Fixed by PR #7168, merged into release/v0.121.3 on 2026-09-26. JP's June "confirmed hex" claim (commit fa98e11db4) was wrong or Composio changed.

SECOND BUG (found 2026-10-28, live-eu): after the signature fix, real deliveries return 202 but are dropped. The ingest route reads `metadata.id` as the event id. Composio V3 envelopes put the event id at the top level (`id`); `metadata` has `trigger_id`, `log_id`, etc. but no `id`. So every real event takes the "No trigger_id/id to route" no-op branch. The dev bridge (`entrypoints/dispatcher_composio.py`) and the acceptance tests inject `metadata.id`, which hides the bug. Symptom: zero `trigger_deliveries` rows for every event subscription, no `[TASK] triggers.dispatch trigger=` lines in worker-queues logs. Also `tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py` reads `metadata.get("id")`.

GKE-era recipe (2026-10-28): New Relic has no data after the GKE move. Use `CLOUDSDK_CORE_ACCOUNT=devbox-vm@...` + kubectl logs on agenta-api-* and agenta-worker-queues-* in live-eu; DB via the psql exec recipe in [[project-cloud-runs-on-gcp-not-aws]]; Composio API from inside the api pod with `$COMPOSIO_API_KEY` (never print it).

Old debug recipe (AWS era), in order:
1. New Relic (see [[newrelic-access]]): `SELECT count(*) FROM Transaction WHERE name LIKE '%ingest_composio_event%' FACET appName, http.statusCode SINCE 7 days ago`. 401 = signature; external call count 1 = the secret was re-fetched, so it got past the timestamp check.
2. API container logs: API logs are NOT in NR Logs. Use `aws ssm send-command --profile production` (needs `aws sso login --profile production`, which Mahmoud runs) on the `live-vps` instance with a read-only `docker logs <api> | grep "TRIGGER SIGNATURE"`.
3. The live Composio webhook registration: run a script inside the api container that GETs `/webhook_subscriptions` and prints URL/version and only the secret length, never the secret.

Unit tests sign their own requests, so they cannot catch a format mismatch with the real provider. See [[verify-fix-against-system-not-finding]].

1. Grep `kubectl logs --since=48h` of every `agenta-runner-*` pod in live-eu, live-us, and stage
   (`staging`, `oss`) with `CLOUDSDK_CORE_ACCOUNT=devbox-vm@...` ([[devbox-vm-service-account]]).
2. Read back from the hit to the `[sessions] stream ... sessionId=` line for model, harness, project.
3. The turn's spans are in the tracing DB: exec into `deploy/agenta-api`, psql on `$POSTGRES_URI_TRACING`
   (sed off `+asyncpg` and `?...`), `select ... from spans where project_id=... and start_time between ...`.
   Chat spans show each model call's duration and error.
4. uvicorn logs access at response START, so a model call the client abandoned before headers leaves no line.

Agenta cloud runs on GCP now. Mahmoud corrected me on 2026-10-15 after I asked him to run `aws sso login` to look up a customer's Stripe customer id: "we are using gcp now, we are not working aws anymore."

**Why:** the AWS notes ([[agenta-cloud-debug-access]], [[project_agenta_cloud_deploy]]) predate the GKE cutover and sent me to dead tooling.

**How to apply:** for any production lookup, use gcloud, not aws. Never suggest `aws sso login`, `rds_connect.sh` or `ec2_connect.sh`.

Production layout (from agenta_cloud `hosting/kubernetes/gcp/`, origin/main, 2026-10-15):
- GCP project `agenta-prod`. Account `mahmoud@agenta.ai`. If gcloud says "Reauthentication failed", Mahmoud must run `gcloud auth login` himself (interactive).
- live-eu: cluster `agenta-prod-eu`, region europe-west3, kube context `gke_agenta-prod_europe-west3_agenta-prod-eu`, namespace `live-eu`, Cloud SQL `agenta-prod-eu-pg-live`, Secret Manager `agenta-prod-eu-live-app-env`, host eu.cloud.agenta.ai.
- live-us: cluster `agenta-prod-us`, region us-east4, kube context `gke_agenta-prod_us-east4_agenta-prod-us`, namespace `live-us`, Cloud SQL `agenta-prod-us-pg-live`, Secret Manager `agenta-prod-us-live-app-env`, host us.cloud.agenta.ai.

- Stripe portal link for an org: same exec, `curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8000/admin/billing/stripe/portals/?organization_id=<id>" -H "Authorization: Access $AGENTA_AUTH_KEY"`. The key stays inside the pod.

"""Trigger dispatcher — asyncio side of the inbound pipeline.

Entity-agnostic: ``dispatch`` runs one already-resolved entity (a
``TriggerSubscription`` from the Composio path, or a ``TriggerSchedule`` from the
cron path) against its bound workflow, dedups on ``event_id``, maps
``inputs_fields`` into the workflow inputs, and records one delivery row. The
``ti_*`` → subscription lookup lives in the worker, not here.

Self-contained so it can run inside its own TaskIQ worker process.
"""

from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Optional, Union
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import uuid_utils.compat as uuid_compat

from oss.src.core.access.dtos import RunOrigin
from oss.src.core.access.principals import (

    missing_principal_error,

from oss.src.core.access.service import AccessService, get_access_service
from oss.src.core.tools.dtos import AgentError
from oss.src.core.shared.dtos import Status
from oss.src.core.triggers.dtos import (
    TRIGGER_CONTEXT_FIELDS,
    SUBSCRIPTION_CONTEXT_FIELDS,
    TriggerDeliveryCreate,
    TriggerDeliveryData,
    TriggerSchedule,
    TriggerSubscription,
)
from oss.src.core.triggers.interfaces import TriggersDAOInterface

log = get_module_logger(__name__)


def _agent_deleted_error() -> AgentError:
    return AgentError(
        code="agent_deleted",
        message="The trigger's agent was deleted, so the trigger is paused.",
        retryable=False,
        next_step="Point the trigger at another agent, then turn it on again.",
    )


class TriggersDispatcher:
    """Resolves and runs one inbound provider event against its bound workflow."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        triggers_dao: TriggersDAOInterface,
        session_claims_dao: TriggerSessionClaimsDAOInterface,
        workflows_service: WorkflowsService,
        run_admission: RunAdmission,
        dispatch_fn: Optional[Callable] = None,
        access_service: Optional[AccessService] = None,
        sharing_service: Optional[SharingService] = None,
    ):
        self.triggers_dao = triggers_dao
        # Admits every fire (the principal and the resolved agent) before the claim.
        self.run_admission = run_admission
        self.session_claims_dao = session_claims_dao
        self.workflows_service = workflows_service
        self._dispatch_fn = dispatch_fn
        # None: the process's registered service (bootstrap_access).
        self._access_service = access_service
        # Every root builds the dispatcher after bootstrap_access().
        self.sharing_service = sharing_service or get_sharing_service()

    @property
    def access_service(self) -> AccessService:
        return self._access_service or get_access_service()

    def _build_context(
        self,
        *,
        event: Dict[str, Any],
        entity: Union[TriggerSubscription, TriggerSchedule],
        project_id: UUID,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        sub_dump = entity.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
        metadata = event.get("metadata") or {}
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        normalized = {
            "event_id": metadata.get("id"),
            "event_type": metadata.get("trigger_slug"),
            "timestamp": now,
            "created_at": now,
            "attributes": event.get("payload"),
        }
        return {
            "event": {
                k: v for k, v in normalized.items() if k in TRIGGER_CONTEXT_FIELDS
            },
            "subscription": {
                k: v for k, v in sub_dump.items() if k in SUBSCRIPTION_CONTEXT_FIELDS
            },
            "scope": {"project_id": str(project_id)},
        }

    async def dispatch_subscription(
        self,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        subscription: TriggerSubscription,
        event_id: str,
        event: Dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Dispatch an inbound provider event for one subscription.

        Subscription-only gates (dedup on the provider event_id, is_valid →
        failed delivery) run here, then the path converges on ``_run``.
        """
        if not subscription.flags.is_active:
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] Subscription %s inactive — skipping",
                subscription.id,
            )
            return

        already_seen = await self.triggers_dao.dedup_seen(
            project_id=project_id,
            subscription_id=subscription.id,
            event_id=event_id,
        )
        if already_seen:
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] Duplicate event %s for subscription %s — skipping",
                event_id,
                subscription.id,
            )
            return

        # Test mode: capture the resolved event as a test delivery and skip the
        # workflow entirely (no binding required). Runs after dedup, before the
        # is_valid gate — a test sub is typically unbound/invalid by design.
        if subscription.flags.is_test:
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] Subscription %s is test — capturing event %s",
                subscription.id,
                event_id,
            )
            context = self._build_context(
                event=event,
                entity=subscription,
                project_id=project_id,
            )
            template = subscription.data.inputs_fields
            inputs = resolve_target_fields(
                template if template is not None else "$", context
            )
            await self._write_subscription_delivery_if_live(
                project_id=project_id,
                user_id=subscription.created_by_id,
                delivery_id=uuid_compat.uuid7(),
                subscription_id=subscription.id,
                schedule_id=None,
                event_id=event_id,
                status=Status(code="200", message="success"),
                data=TriggerDeliveryData(
                    event_key=subscription.data.event_key,
                    inputs=inputs if isinstance(inputs, dict) else {"value": inputs},
                    is_test=True,
                ),
            )
            return

        # is_valid is NOT a silent skip: write a failed delivery so the user sees
        # why nothing ran, and never invoke the workflow.
        if not subscription.flags.is_valid:
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] Subscription %s is invalid — failed delivery",
                subscription.id,
            )
            await self._write_subscription_delivery_if_live(
                project_id=project_id,
                user_id=subscription.created_by_id,
                delivery_id=uuid_compat.uuid7(),
                subscription_id=subscription.id,
                schedule_id=None,
                event_id=event_id,
                status=Status(code="409", message="failed"),
                data=TriggerDeliveryData(
                    event_key=subscription.data.event_key,
                    references=subscription.data.references,
                    error="Subscription is invalid (provider connection revoked or unsynced)",
                ),
            )
            return

        await self._run(
            project_id=project_id,
            entity=subscription,
            event_id=event_id,
            event=event,
        )

    async def dispatch_schedule(
        self,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        schedule: TriggerSchedule,
        event_id: str,
        event: Dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Dispatch a cron tick for one schedule (no provider/validity gates).

        Dedups on the (schedule, tick) event_id like ``dispatch_subscription``: the task
        is retried on error, so without this a failure after the workflow's side effects
        landed would re-invoke it.
        """
        if not schedule.flags.is_active:
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] Schedule %s inactive — skipping",
                schedule.id,
            )
            return

        already_seen = await self.triggers_dao.dedup_seen_schedule(
            project_id=project_id,
            schedule_id=schedule.id,
            event_id=event_id,
        )
        if already_seen:
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] Duplicate event %s for schedule %s — skipping",
                event_id,
                schedule.id,
            )
            return

        await self._run(
            project_id=project_id,
            entity=schedule,
            event_id=event_id,
            event=event,
        )

    async def _run(
        self,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        entity: Union[TriggerSubscription, TriggerSchedule],
        event_id: str,
        event: Dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Shared path once a subscription/schedule is cleared to fire: claim the
        delivery row, resolve inputs + references, invoke the bound workflow, and
        complete the delivery.

        The claim is the ONLY thing that authorizes an invoke: it is an atomic
        ``INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING ... RETURNING`` on the same unique key
        (project_id, subscription_id|schedule_id, event_id) the caller's earlier
        dedup pre-check reads. Two concurrent ticks/deliveries for the same event
        both reach `_run`, but only the one whose INSERT lands may invoke — the
        other's claim returns false and it returns immediately. Every subsequent
        write in this method UPDATEs that same claimed row by id (never inserts),
        so a delivery-write failure after a successful invoke cannot look like "no
        row exists" to a retry and cause a re-invoke.
        """
        is_subscription = isinstance(entity, TriggerSubscription)

        # No principal (created by a pod before M2, or a creatorless row the backfill
        # paused): refuse and pause. The principal is never rebuilt from created_by_id.
        if entity.principal is None:
            await self._refuse(
                project_id=project_id,
                entity=entity,
                event_id=event_id,
                reason="missing_principal",
                error=missing_principal_error(next_step="Create the trigger again."),
            )
            return

        delivery_id = uuid_compat.uuid7()
        session_id = uuid4().hex
        user_id = entity.created_by_id
        kind = (
            SessionTriggerKind.subscription
            if is_subscription
            else SessionTriggerKind.schedule
        )

        # Build the request and resolve its target BEFORE the claim, so the principal
        # is checked against the revision that will run. A build or resolution failure
        # is still recorded on a claimed delivery (400), as before.
        delivery_data = TriggerDeliveryData(session_id=session_id)
        request: Optional[WorkflowServiceRequest] = None
        failure: Optional[str] = None
        target = None
        try:
            context = self._build_context(
                event=event,
                entity=entity,
                project_id=project_id,
            )
            template = entity.data.inputs_fields
            inputs = resolve_target_fields(
                template if template is not None else "$", context
            )
            references = (
                {
                    k: ref.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
                    for k, ref in entity.data.references.items()
                }
                if entity.data.references
                else None
            )
            if not references:
                raise ValueError("Entity has no bound workflow reference")
            selector = (
                entity.data.selector.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
                if entity.data.selector
                else None
            )
            delivery_data = TriggerDeliveryData(
                session_id=session_id,
                event_key=entity.data.event_key,
                references=entity.data.references,
                inputs=inputs if isinstance(inputs, dict) else {"value": inputs},
            )
            request = WorkflowServiceRequest(
                references=references,
                selector=selector,
                session_id=session_id,
                data=WorkflowRequestData(
                    inputs=inputs if isinstance(inputs, dict) else {"value": inputs},
                ),
            )
            target = await self.workflows_service.resolve_request_target(
                project_id=project_id,
                request=request,
            )
            if target is None:
                raise ValueError("The bound workflow reference resolves to no revision")
        except Exception as e:
            failure = str(e)

        if failure is None and target is not None and target.archived:
            await self._refuse(
                project_id=project_id,
                entity=entity,
                event_id=event_id,
                reason="agent_deleted",
                error=_agent_deleted_error(),
            )
            return

        envelope = None
        if failure is None:
            envelope = stored_work_envelope(
                principal=entity.principal,
                organization_id=await self._organization_id(project_id=project_id),
                project_id=project_id,
                origin=(
                    RunOrigin.SUBSCRIPTION if is_subscription else RunOrigin.SCHEDULE
                ),
                origin_id=str(entity.id),
                created_by_id=entity.created_by_id,
            )
            # The target resolved above is the one checked and the one that runs
            # (the stored `artifact_id` is a pause index, never read here). The
            # admission logs a refusal with the run context (origin, trigger id).
            try:
                await self.run_admission.admit(
                    envelope=envelope,
                    session_id=None,
                    agent_artifact_id=target.artifact_id,
                    REDACTED,
                )
            except AdmissionDenied as denied:
                decision = denied.decision
                await self._refuse(
                    project_id=project_id,
                    entity=entity,
                    event_id=event_id,
                    reason="access_denied",
                    error=access_denied_error(
                        decision=decision,
                        principal_kind=entity.principal.kind,
                        project_id=project_id,
                    ),
                )
                return

        claimed = await self.session_claims_dao.claim_trigger_delivery(
            project_id=project_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            event_id=event_id,
            session_id=session_id,
            attribution=SessionTriggerAttribution(
                configuration_id=entity.id,
                kind=kind,
                delivery_id=delivery_id,
            ),
            access=self.sharing_service.initial_policy(
                principal=entity.principal,
                origin=(
                    RunOrigin.SUBSCRIPTION if is_subscription else RunOrigin.SCHEDULE
                ),
                sender_user_id=None,
                kind=SharedItemKind.SESSION,
            ),
        )
        if not claimed:
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] claim lost for entity=%s event=%s — already "
                "claimed/delivered, skipping invoke",
                entity.id,
                event_id,
            )
            return

        if failure is not None:
            await self._complete_delivery(
                project_id=project_id,
                delivery_id=delivery_id,
                status=Status(code="400", message="failed"),
                data=delivery_data.model_copy(update={"error": failure}),
            )
            await self._abandon_claimed_session(
                project_id=project_id, session_id=session_id
            )
            return

        if self._dispatch_fn is not None:
            # Detached completion means the runner accepted ownership. The API has no durable
            # callback for the run's later terminal outcome, so this delivery remains 202.
            try:
                run_id = await self._dispatch_fn(
                    project_id=project_id,
                    user_id=user_id,
                    request=request,
                    envelope=envelope,
                )
            except Exception as e:
                log.error("[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] detached invoke failed: %s", e)
                await self._complete_delivery(
                    project_id=project_id,
                    delivery_id=delivery_id,
                    status=Status(code="500", message="failed"),
                    data=delivery_data.model_copy(update={"error": str(e)}),
                )
                await self._abandon_claimed_session(
                    project_id=project_id, session_id=session_id
                )
                raise
            await self._complete_delivery(
                project_id=project_id,
                delivery_id=delivery_id,
                status=Status(code="202", message="dispatched"),
                data=delivery_data.model_copy(update={"result": {"run_id": run_id}}),
            )
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] detached dispatch entity=%s event=%s run_id=%s",
                entity.id,
                event_id,
                run_id,
            )
            return

        try:
            response = await self.workflows_service.invoke_workflow(
                project_id=project_id,
                user_id=user_id,
                request=request,
                envelope=envelope,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            log.error("[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] invoke failed: %s", e, exc_info=True)
            await self._complete_delivery(
                project_id=project_id,
                delivery_id=delivery_id,
                status=Status(code="500", message="failed"),
                data=delivery_data.model_copy(update={"error": str(e)}),
            )
            raise

        status_obj = getattr(response, "status", None)
        status_code = getattr(status_obj, "code", None)
        outputs = getattr(response, "outputs", None) or getattr(
            getattr(response, "data", None), "outputs", None
        )

        if status_code not in (None, 200):
            await self._complete_delivery(
                project_id=project_id,
                delivery_id=delivery_id,
                status=Status(code=str(status_code), message="failed"),
                data=delivery_data.model_copy(
                    update={
                        "error": getattr(status_obj, "message", None)
                        or "Workflow failed",
                        "result": {
                            "trace_id": getattr(response, "trace_id", None),
                            "span_id": getattr(response, "span_id", None),
                        },
                    }
                ),
            )
            return

        await self._complete_delivery(
            project_id=project_id,
            delivery_id=delivery_id,
            status=Status(code="200", message="success"),
            data=delivery_data.model_copy(
                update={
                    "result": {
                        "trace_id": getattr(response, "trace_id", None),
                        "span_id": getattr(response, "span_id", None),
                        "outputs": outputs,
                    }
                }
            ),
        )
        log.info(
            "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] dispatch complete entity=%s event=%s status=200",
            entity.id,
            event_id,
        )

    async def _organization_id(self, *, project_id: UUID) -> UUID:
        organization_id = await self.access_service.project_organization_id(
            project_id=project_id
        )
        if organization_id is None:
            raise ValueError(f"project {project_id} has no organization")
        return organization_id

    async def _refuse(
        self,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        entity: Union[TriggerSubscription, TriggerSchedule],
        event_id: str,
        reason: str,
        error: AgentError,
    ) -> None:
        """A refused delivery (status failed, `error` the message, `error_details` the
        envelope) and the trigger paused, in one DAO transaction. A repeated event
        writes nothing."""

        is_subscription = isinstance(entity, TriggerSubscription)
        await self.triggers_dao.refuse_delivery(
            project_id=project_id,
            user_id=entity.created_by_id,
            delivery=TriggerDeliveryCreate(
                id=uuid_compat.uuid7(),
                subscription_id=entity.id if is_subscription else None,
                schedule_id=None if is_subscription else entity.id,
                event_id=event_id,
                status=Status(code="403", message="failed"),
                data=TriggerDeliveryData(
                    event_key=entity.data.event_key,
                    references=entity.data.references,
                    error=error.message,
                    error_details=error,
                ),
            ),
            reason=reason,
        )
        log.info(
            "[triggers] paused",
            trigger_kind="subscription" if is_subscription else "schedule",
            trigger_id=str(entity.id),
            project_id=str(project_id),
            principal_kind=entity.principal.kind.value if entity.principal else None,
            principal_id=str(entity.principal.id) if entity.principal else None,
            reason=reason,
        )

    async def _write_subscription_delivery_if_live(
        self,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        user_id: Optional[UUID],
        delivery_id: UUID,
        subscription_id: Optional[UUID],
        schedule_id: Optional[UUID],
        event_id: str,
        status: Status,
        data: TriggerDeliveryData,
    ) -> None:
        written = await self.triggers_dao.write_subscription_delivery_if_live(
            project_id=project_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            delivery=TriggerDeliveryCreate(
                id=delivery_id,
                subscription_id=subscription_id,
                schedule_id=schedule_id,
                event_id=event_id,
                status=status,
                data=data,
            ),
        )
        if written is None:
            # The subscription went inactive/was deleted between the dispatcher's
            # gate check and this write — not an error, but a silent no-op here
            # otherwise looks identical to a normal write from the logs alone.
            log.info(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] delivery write skipped — subscription %s "
                "is no longer live/active (event=%s)",
                subscription_id,
                event_id,
            )

    async def _abandon_claimed_session(
        self,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        session_id: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Soft-delete the session_streams row `_run`'s claim inserted, when dispatch
        fails before a turn ever starts. Its `flags` are NULL at claim time — the
        orphan sweep only matches `is_alive: true` — so left alone it becomes a
        permanent, un-sweepable phantom session (P0-3)."""
        try:
            await self.session_claims_dao.abandon_claimed_session(
                project_id=project_id, session_id=session_id
            )
        except Exception:
            log.error(
                "[TRIGGERS DISPATCHER] failed to abandon claimed session=%s",
                session_id,
                exc_info=True,
            )

    async def _complete_delivery(
        self,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        delivery_id: UUID,
        status: Status,
        data: TriggerDeliveryData,
    ) -> None:
        """Complete a row `_run` already claimed — an UPDATE by id, never a fresh
        INSERT, so a write failure here cannot look like "no delivery yet" to a
        retry (see `_run`'s claim-then-update contract)."""
        await self.triggers_dao.update_delivery(
            project_id=project_id,
            delivery_id=delivery_id,
            status=status,
            data=data,
        )

content.text:
The Composio side works now. The event reaches our dispatcher with its data. The agent still gets nothing from the event, because the automation only sends the instruction text the user typed.

**What happens to an event today:**
1. `ingest_composio_event` checks the signature and normalizes the webhook. It puts Composio's `data` under `payload`. This part is correct.
2. The dispatcher builds a context of `event.attributes` (the GitHub payload), `event.event_type` and `event.event_id`. It also adds subscription fields and the project id ([dispatcher.py `_build_context`](api/oss/src/tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py)).
3. The dispatcher then builds the workflow inputs from the subscription's `inputs_fields` template, using `resolve_target_fields(template, context)`. The agent only sees event data if the template points at it with a selector such as `$.event.attributes.body`.
4. On the release branch, the automation form saves a fixed text with no selectors: `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<your instruction>"}]}`. The selectors find nothing to fill, and the event data is dropped.

**Why the template has no event fields:** event automations use the schedule's `MessageComposer` ([MessageComposer.tsx](web/packages/agenta-entity-ui/src/gatewayTrigger/drawers/schedule/MessageComposer.tsx)), which is a plain textarea. The old subscription form had an event field picker that inserted `{{event.attributes...}}` tokens. Commit `89c2d80c39` (2026-09-08, "delete the trigger forms the automation drawer replaced") deleted it. The new automation form never got the picker back. The helper that compiles those tokens, `compileMessageTemplate`, still exists, but no screen calls it now.

So every event automation built in the new form runs the agent with only the instruction. "Review this PR" arrives with no PR attached.

**I did not check your specific run.** The permission system blocked my read-only query on the production tracing database for trace `4472f944105d461a8ca762c56ef1c9bf`. To confirm, look at that run's first user message: it should contain only the instruction text. The delivery row's `data.inputs` should show the same thing.

**Two ways to fix it:**
- **Option 1, backend (my recommendation):** for subscription runs, the dispatcher always adds the event to the agent's message, as a second text part with the event type and the payload as JSON. Every existing event automation starts working without being edited, and users do not need to learn tokens. The cost is that large payloads, such as a full GitHub PR body, go into every prompt. We can cap the size.
- **Option 2, frontend:** put the event field picker back into the instruction field, so users insert `{{event.attributes.pull_request.html_url}}` and similar tokens. This gives users precise control. But every existing automation stays broken until someone edits it, and non-technical users must know which fields to pick.

content.text:
Yes, we have it, and our API already fetches it. Each Composio event type comes with a schema that lists its fields. Each field has a name, a type and a short description written for people. The UI just does not show this information.

**Where it comes from.** `GET /triggers/catalog/providers/composio/integrations/{integration}/events/{event_key}` calls Composio's `/triggers_types/{slug}`. The response puts the schema in `payload` ([catalog.py `_parse_event_detail`](api/oss/src/core/triggers/providers/composio/catalog.py)). No frontend code reads that field today.

**What it looks like.** I fetched real schemas from Composio:

| Event | Fields (with Composio's own descriptions) |
|---|---|
| GitHub pull request | `title`, `description` ("A detailed description of the pull request"), `url`, `number`, `createdBy`, `action`, `createdAt` |
| GitHub issue added | the same set, plus `issue_id` |
| Gmail new message | `sender`, `subject`, `message_text`, `to`, `attachment_list`, `thread_id`, … |
| Slack receive message | `text`, `user`, `channel`, `files`, `ts`, … |
| Linear issue created | `action`, `type`, `url`, and a nested `data` object |

The flat ones are already easy to read. A few, like Linear, put the useful fields inside a nested object. For those, the picker must open one level down.

**What the UI could show.** Under the instruction box, show the event's fields as chips: "Title", "Description", "URL", "Created by". Each chip shows its description on hover. A click inserts a pill into the message. The pill is stored as `$.event.attributes.title`, the selector format the dispatcher already resolves. The helper that builds this format (`compileMessageTemplate`) still exists and has tests, so the storage side is already done. The work is the chips and the pills in the composer.

**One thing I did not check.** The schema describes the event. I have not compared it to a real delivery, because the permission system blocked my read of your production trace. If Composio's `data` uses different keys from the schema, the pills would come out empty. Before we build, we should compare one real GitHub delivery to its schema.

**My recommendation is to build both parts:**
- **The field picker.** Users see what the event holds, in plain words, and choose what goes into the message.
- **A backend fallback.** If the instruction uses no event field, the dispatcher attaches the whole event to the message. This fixes the automations that already exist and covers users who never click a chip. Without it, every current event automation stays broken until someone edits it.

How the parts map to the data we have:

- **Header.** The header names the event in plain words, with the integration's icon and the agent that runs.
- **Field cards.** Each card is one field from the event's schema, which Composio gives us. The card text is Composio's description. The card names are shorter labels: "Link" stands for `url` and "Opened by" stands for `createdBy`. - **Preview.** The preview fills the pills with values from the last real delivery for this automation. A new automation has no delivery yet, so the preview would show the schema's example values or the field names.

# Communicating with Mahmoud

Doing the work is half the job, and communicating it is the other half. Mahmoud reads the
chat to make decisions, so a correct result written up as a data dump is a failure. He has
said more than once that he would switch models over output he cannot read. Treat every
writeup as part of the deliverable.

For sentence style, load `~/.claude/skills/plain-writing/SKILL.md` and follow it. This
skill adds the rules about the reader, the structure, and the process.

## The reader

- Mahmoud is a senior Python developer and architect. He is a beginner in TypeScript and
  frontend work. Explain frontend ideas in terms he can map from the backend.
- He did not read the PR. He does not know the shorthand you built up this session, and he
  does not care in which order you found things.
- For docs, the reader is a stranger with a job, not a teammate. Never assume what they
  know. Phrases such as "the part teams get wrong" or "the first question people ask" are
  banned.

## Structure: context first, then a story

Use this order:

1. Context. What the thing is and why it exists. A reader with no session context must be
   able to follow from here.
2. The choices or parts, one at a time. For each one: how it works, what the user installs
   or does, where things live, and the trade-off.
3. How they combine, with a concrete live example.
4. Limits and gaps.
5. The plan or the options, with a recommendation.

Apply these rules across the whole piece:

- Give each section one axis. Pick the reader's natural questions ("how does it run
  locally?", "what do I install?", "what breaks?") and answer them in order. Do not spread
  one topic across three sections.
- Write headings as plain signposts that state the content. A heading is not a sentence and
  not a clever label.
- Explain how things work today before you describe a change. Show before and after with
  concrete examples: real data shapes and real code.
- If an explanation is short and complicated, rewrite it long and simple.
- Give every decision its reasoning: the problem, the options, the trade-offs, the choice,
  and why. "We do X" with no reason is a review comment waiting to happen.

## Banned patterns

These rules are absolute. Repeat them in every subagent brief.

- No em dashes. Use a period and a new sentence, parentheses, or a semicolon. Check the
  places where they come back: term definitions, trade-off lists, asides, and list item
  separators. The count must be zero.
- No slang: soak, bikeshed, yak-shaving, greenfield, and similar words. Say the plain thing,
  for example "after it has run in real use for a while without problems".
- No drama: "precise and damning", "the one that bit you", "say the word", cute closing
  lines, narrative tension. Debugging and status updates are flat: what happened, what it
  means, what is next.
- No undefined terms. Define every term on first use (runner, vault, sandbox, harness,
  overlay, and any other domain term).
- No bare internal labels. Never use a code such as F-7, C2, Tier 1 or P0 without restating
  it in plain words, every time. He does not remember labels between messages. Prefer names
  that describe themselves, such as "must fix before enabling".
- No meta text in the body. Never write "amended after review", "added per finding", or
  "updated per X" in a doc or report. Provenance goes in PR comments or an appendix.
- Use bold and bullets only when they help quick reading. A wall of bullets should be prose.

## Two lists: what I do, what you do

Always separate "what I will do" from "what you need to do" as two explicit lists. Do not
mix your actions and his actions in one paragraph.

## When he is tired or confused

Drop all compression. Use short sentences with one idea each, numbered steps, and say who
does what at each step. A status update in the middle of the work follows the same rules.

## Questions

- In strategy, brainstorm, and thinking-out-loud conversations, ask one open prose question
  at a time. Do not use multi-select menus. If options help, mention them inline as
  suggestions.
- Use structured multiple choice only for a real, discrete fork in execution work.

## Verify before you assert

- Never write an instruction or claim you have not checked against the code, the config
  file, or the actual behavior. Fluent, confident, wrong instructions cost the reader hours.
  If you cannot verify a claim, cut it.
- Before you hand over docs, run an adversarial pass: a fresh check whose job is to find
  what is still wrong against this skill and `plain-writing`. A self-assessment is not
  evidence.

## Subagent output is your output

- Read everything a subagent wrote (PR body, design doc, report) against this skill before
  you tell Mahmoud it is ready. A rewrite round after he reads it counts as a failure.
- Naming this skill in a brief is not enough. Copy the reader profile and the banned
  patterns above into the brief, word for word.

## PR descriptions

The `write-pr-description` skill, when the repo has it, holds the full procedure. These
rules always apply:

1. Lead with the concrete symptom: what was broken, from the user's point of view.
2. Then the fix in plain words, with a concrete before and after. Show the real data shapes
   when a transformation changed.
3. Then a short section on tests and notes.
4. Add a "How to review" section that walks the diff in reading order.
5. Leave inline comments on the subtle hunks to explain the reason a reviewer would
   otherwise have to work out.

Cut vague bullets that restate the diff, checkbox theater, and "Summary" boilerplate. The
title states the actual change, for example
`fix(api): map OpenInference tool definitions into real tool objects`.
